text:
jess: Heads up — after the autobatch tuning merge (PR #4921) we started seeing a steady memory residency increase on several longctx instances. Not full OOM yet but growth linearly over ~10k requests.
liam: saw that on staging too. Reproducer with seqlen 8k/12k shows resident set creeping up per request. CI perf job flagged endpoint mem-per-request +38%. link: https://ci.internal/runs/7852
zara: bisected this morning, pointing at commit ab12c3f (kernel-router: adjust batch boundary + reserve pages for slab prefetch).
jess: yeah that commit introduced a pre-reserve of 2 pages per slab stripe to try to reduce prefetch stalls. Looks like we forgot to decrement when eviction wins the race.
kevin: can you paste the quick pmap/top output?
zara: pmap snapshot from repro VM after 5k requests:
```
00007f8e3d000000   12K r---- /app/lib/kv_slab.so
00007f8e3d003000  512K rw--- [ anon ]
00007f8e3d083000  1.4M rw--- [ anon ]  <-- growing region (page residency increasing)
```
liam: heap profile (pprof) top lines:
```
1.7GB  42.1%  runtime/mmap
600MB  14.8%  kv/cache:reserve_pages
420MB  10.4%  autobatch:batch_window_alloc
```
jess: that reserve_pages is the red flag — should not be accumulating like that. In prod we see steady +200MB after ~30 minutes on our canary.
ci-bot: CI perf check failed for job 7852: mem-per-request delta +38% (threshold 20%).
deploy-bot: Rollout for channel runtime-2026-03-17 halted due to perf regression.
kevin: hypothesis: when batch boundary moves, we create short-lived prefetched slabs and increment slab.page_residency counter but eviction path expects exact window tokens and sometimes misses the decrement, leaving pages pinned. Edge is sequence-length sensitive since larger seq triggers prefetch of larger contiguous pages.
zara: repro script attached in thread: `scripts/repro_kv_residency.sh` (runs local workload and prints pmap every 1000 requests).
jess: tested a quick patch that move decrement under a compare-and-swap and it stops the leak in the repro. Patch: `diff --git a/kv/scheduler.c b/kv/scheduler.c 
@@
-    slab->page_residency += n;
+    if (__sync_bool_compare_and_swap(&slab->status, EXPECTED, UPDATED))
+        slab->page_residency += n;
`
liam: can you open an internal PR? we need either revert ab12c3f or fast fix on the eviction path. Which is lower risk?
jess: revert is safe but blocks perf gains from autobatch. The minimal fix to ensure decrement symmetry seems small. I'm pushing a hotfix PR that also adds a unit test for race between pre-reserve and evict.
kevin: make sure the fix also updates metrics so we can graph `kv.page_residency` per-slab and alert on >200MB sustained increase.
zara: added extra CI test variant to stress seqlen=8k/12k paths; it catches the regression locally.
liam: timeline: if hotfix PR passes CI we can un-halt rollout and resume canaries. If not, we revert ab12c3f. Either way let's block main rollout until next midnight.
jess: patch PR: https://git.internal/r/PR/4975 — includes changelog and test. Please review, cc @kevin @zara.
kevin: reviewing now. Also let's add a perf gate for mem-per-request in CI to fail earlier on merges touching kernel-router/kv.
jess: +1 on perf gate. I'll add a small flamegraph unit that runs in CI with representative seqlen distribution.
liam: thanks everyone. Keep updates here — if we get a green CI, we can re-enable canary. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Manual hold placed on rollout runtime-2026-03-17 by jess. Reason: mem regression failure.
